item.title: Baz Luhrmann’s EPiC tribute to The King
item.description: Directed by acclaimed Australian director Baz Luhrmann, “EPiC: Elvis Presley in Concert” presents previously lost and unseen footage of the King of Rock and Roll. Source: Australian Catholics.

item.title: Ex-intelligence chief arrested over Sri Lankan bombings
item.description: Families of victims of Sri Lanka’s 2019 Easter Sunday bombings have expressed renewed hope for justice after police arrested a former top intelligence official over the coordinated attacks that killed 279 people. Source: UCA News.

item.title: Vatican’s top diplomat urges push for Ukraine peace
item.description: The Vatican’s top diplomat, Archbishop Paul Gallagher, has urged the international community to take “concrete steps” towards peace in Ukraine. Source: Vatican News.

item.title: Lenten retreat offers women a space to ‘stop, rest, and receive’
item.description: Each year, more women are choosing to step away from the noise of everyday life and treat the annual Women’s Lenten Retreat in Sydney as a kind of pilgrimage. Source: The Catholic Weekly.

item.title: Grape day for winery established by the Jesuits 175 years ago
item.description: The annual blessing of one of Australia’s oldest operating wineries took place in the Clare Valley on February 20. Source: The Southern Cross.

item.title: Albanese maintains uncompromising stance on ISIS families
item.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has voiced compassion for the 23 Australian children detained in Syria, but remains defiant against their desperate pleas to return home. Source: 9news.com.au.

item.title: Commissioner holds private meeting with survivors and their families
item.description: Royal Commissioner Virginia Bell yesterday held a private meeting with victims, survivors and their families from the Bondi massacre. Source: Sydney Morning Herald.

item.title: Angelic encounter can’t be replaced by chatbot: Bishop Varden
item.description: There is a “prophetic challenge” facing the Church in today’s world with the rise of “digital, artificial” media, according to Bishop Erik Varden, who is conducting the Lenten spiritual retreat at the Vatican. Source: Crux.

item.title: ACT’s assisted dying scheme sees 14 people die in three months
item.description: Fourteen people have died by voluntary assisted dying in the first three months of the ACT scheme. Source: Canberra Times.
